\[
L(p) = \begin{cases} k & p \text{ in the } k\text{th component of } F \\ 0 & p \notin F \end{cases},
\qquad F = \{\, p : Y(p) \ge 128 \,\}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(F\): The foreground pixels
- \(L(p)\): The label of pixel p
- \(Y(p)\): The brightness of pixel p

Two foreground pixels belong to the same component when a path of foreground pixels joins them, each step to one of 4 or 8 neighbors. The components are numbered by their first pixel in a row by row scan, as scipy.ndimage.label and scikit-image number them. Rosenfeld and Pfaltz describe labeling in two passes over the image. PixelNexus follows each component from its first pixel instead, which gives the same labels. In the color view, label k gets the hue k times 137.5 degrees, the golden angle, so neighboring numbers get very different colors. The gray view shows label k as 255 k / n for n components.
